page: OVHcloud r3-32 is a memory-optimized virtual instance powered by the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 4 dedicated physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.3 GHz, with one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading enabled. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware cryptographic instruction sets such as AES and SHA-NI.

Hardware allocations provide a total of 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage features an integrated 100 GB NVMe SSD, providing low-latency disk access directly on the host node. The platform does not bundle discrete GPU accelerators, relying purely on host CPU compute, and is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default.

Benchmark data demonstrates balanced performance across memory and general compute metrics. In raw CPU benchmarks, the r3-32 achieves a strong single-core stress-ng result of 3,077.24, alongside a multi-core score of 12,261.5 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,003.0. Memory throughput remains solid with 120.0 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 74.19 GB/sec for uncached writes. Redis throughput reaches 9.91 million SET operations per second, matching expected performance profiles for in-memory systems.

Tradeoffs center around network-bound operations and heavy vectorized processing. Static web serving throughput tested at 4.42 GB/sec, placing it in the lower quartile, in part reflecting the 1 Gbps network baseline. Additionally, the instance lacks advanced vector sets like AVX-512 and AMX, making medium-to-large LLM processing inefficient, as shown by prompt processing rates of 21.45 tokens/sec on 7B parameter models. Given its dedicated core layout and dense 8 GB per vCPU ratio, the server offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for in-memory caching tiers, relational database instances, and data-intensive backend workloads.
description: OVHcloud r3-32 is a memory-optimized instance built on x86_64 AMD EPYC processors running on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores at 2.3 GHz (1 thread per core), 32.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 100 GB local NVMe SSD. The instance lacks discrete GPUs and provides a 1 Gbps network baseline. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core compute performance alongside stable multi-core and memory subsystem throughput, reaching 9.91 million Redis SET operations per second and 120.0 GB/sec large-block read bandwidth. Tradeoffs include modest web serving throughput and the absence of AVX-512 instructions, which constrains vectorized and AI compute tasks. With an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, r3-32 offers a cost-effective platform for database hosting, Redis caches, and data-processing tasks.
